notes.text: Mention @Claude in the team chat and a Claude Code session answers in the same thread, using your workspace (Settings → Workspace → Claude in chat)
The "Meeting detected" card now shows within about a second of a Zoom or Google Meet call starting, instead of after a few seconds.
Dictate: click the Recent dictations heading to fold the list away or open it again; Hotsauce remembers your choice.
Chrome extension 0.9.0 with the new Hotsauce icon
Files: PDF tools. Combine PDFs, reorder, turn and remove pages, split into parts, shrink for email, make scans searchable, and redact. Each result is saved as a new PDF beside the original.
Drop PDFs on the Hotsauce icon in the Dock to add them to Files and open them in PDF tools. Make searchable uses your Mac's own text reading.
A refreshed Hotsauce icon in the browser tab, the app, installed app icons, the Chrome extension and hotsauce.work
A new app icon on a dark tile, with the refreshed bottle in the menu bar
Calls in Chrome and other browsers, like Google Meet, are now noticed. A "Meeting detected" card appears at the top right with one Take notes button that records both sides.
A new meeting no longer offers "Meet tab + mic", which couldn't hear the call there. "Any app on this Mac" records both sides of a Google Meet.
Present any doc as slides from its top bar: split slides with a line of three dashes, or at each heading, and add speaker notes with a "Notes:" line
Presenter view shows the next slide, your notes, a timer and the clock while a second window shows the slides; L turns on a laser pointer, B blacks out the screen
Draft slides (Command-K) asks the AI for a deck from the doc you're reading and saves it as a new doc beside it
Download slides as PDF, one wide page per slide
Present puts the slides full screen on your external display and keeps presenter view on the laptop; View → Present (⌘⌥P)
The installer window now says "Pour it in, apply liberally".
Download any doc or meeting note as Word or PDF from its Share menu or ⌘K, in your team's fonts and colours with your logo on page one
File → Export… (⌘⇧E) saves the open doc as Word or PDF, with the format picked in the save window

The Chrome extension opens a setup page when you install it: connect to your workspace, pin the icon, and try it on a test Meet call, each ticked off by itself. The same page holds its settings (workspace, keyboard shortcut, version, updates) under Options.
The extension's popup links to Settings and How it works.
Meetings → Chrome extension says whether the extension is found in this browser, when a newer version is ready, and how to take notes on a call, with troubleshooting and how it fits with the Mac app.
Getting started on Today offers the Chrome extension in Chrome on a computer.
Help → Chrome Extension… opens the extension page.

The Hotsauce menu now has Switch Workspace, Open at Login, Show in Menu Bar and Restart Hotsauce. ⌘Q keeps Hotsauce running in the menu bar so dictation and reminders keep working; Quit Completely (⌥⌘Q) quits.
A new Help menu with the help center, keyboard shortcuts, feedback, setup and the code on GitHub.
Finds new versions soon after your Mac wakes from sleep, not only every few hours.
Hotsauce → Check for Updates… checks right away and tells you whether you're up to date, or offers Restart Now when a new version is ready.
About Hotsauce links to the source code on GitHub.
Screenshots no longer ask for Screen Recording when it's already on. If macOS still refuses, the window says exactly what to do and has a Quit and Reopen button.
On an iPad with reduced motion turned on, the History panel no longer covers the doc's top bar.

Share on a screenshot (the corner preview, the editor, or File → Share Screenshot) uploads it and copies a link. Anyone can open the link for 30 days, or only signed-in members when your organization keeps links private.
Settings → This Mac → Screenshots lets you press a new screenshot shortcut, choose the folder, and pick whether a capture is copied, saved and previewed.
Edit on a screenshot opens an editor with arrows, rectangles, ellipses, text, a highlighter, numbered steps, redaction and crop. Everything stays editable and undoable.
Redact blacks out what's underneath for good in what you copy, save or share, and Copy Text skips it.
Copy Text copies the words in a screenshot.

Save writes your changes over the screenshot. Closing the editor or quitting saves them too, and if a save fails you're told and the changes stay open. Once saved, the edited picture also replaces the original on the clipboard if you haven't copied anything else.
File → Edit Last Screenshot and Recent Screenshots reopen your last five shots with their layers still editable.
The welcome tour mentions What's new in the account menu
A new Mac app version is offered within about ten minutes of coming out, instead of up to six hours later.
Your Google account picture is your profile photo until you add your own.
Your teammates' photos show beside their names in People, comments, check-ins and whiteboards.
The account menu has Edit pinned apps, What's new and, on a Mac, Get the Mac app.
A small pepper keeps you company at the bottom of the left bar and hops when you finish a task or a recording. Turn it off in Settings, Appearance.
Switching tools now sends a liquid ripple across the whole window, bending the page like water as it passes.

Screen breaks: turn on Breaks in the account menu (or from the Getting started tile) for a reminder to look away from the screen. You choose how often, how long, a breathing circle, clouds or waves, an end chime and working hours in Settings → General. Breaks wait while you record or are in a meeting, and time away counts as a break.
Screen breaks show over every display, above all apps, even with the Hotsauce window closed. They wait while you dictate or record a call, and a locked or sleeping Mac counts as a break.
A short welcome tour the first time you open Hotsauce on a computer; take it again any time from your account menu
Settings → Hotsauce 101: what every app is for, with a short video of each
For you and Tables now have their own cards and videos on hotsauce.work
The tour and Hotsauce 101 show in the Mac app window too
A few hot sauce surprises are now hidden around the app. 🌶
An address that leads nowhere now says so, with a button back to Docs.
Something spicy hides in the Hotsauce menu.
Press ⌥⇧4 to take a screenshot: drag for an area, click a window for that window, or click the desktop for the whole screen. Esc cancels.
The size in pixels follows the pointer while you choose.
A screenshot is copied at once and saved to Pictures → Hotsauce Screenshots.
A small preview shows in the corner for 7 seconds; hover to keep it, Copy, Pin, Close, or drag it into another app as a file.
Take Screenshot is also in the File menu and the menu bar menu.
A new look, "Follow the sun": Hotsauce turns light at sunrise and dark at sunset where you are. Pick By sun in the account menu or Follow the sun in Settings → Appearance.
Files: a file that is set to delete itself shows the date on its row, with a Keep button to stop it.
Today: a sky behind your greeting changes from dawn to day to dusk to night, in your theme's colours, with the sun where it really is or the moon in its real phase.
Today: sunrise, sunset and hours of daylight under the greeting, using your weather place or your team's city.
Today: clouds, rain, snow and fog from the current weather drift lightly across the sky; it stays still with "reduce motion".
Today: pick Sky, Sun path or Off in Edit Today or Settings → General → Today's sky.
Click the logo at the top of the left bar to widen it, so every icon has its name beside it. Click again to narrow it.
Rest the pointer on an app in the left bar to see what it is for and its shortcut.
Settings, music and feedback moved into the account menu at the bottom of the left bar, which also switches between light and dark and links to keyboard shortcuts and help.
Add a photo of yourself from the account menu or Settings.
The account menu shows which version you are running.
The account menu shows the Mac app's version too.
Appearance has its own page in Settings, right under General.
Weather in Settings and on Today names the town you're in when you share your location.
Switching tools plays a soft ripple from your click (Settings → Appearance turns it off; skipped when your device reduces motion).
An optional quiet tick when switching tools, off by default, silent while anything is recording.
Play music / Pause music in the menu bar menu, and a Music menu with the four tracks.
The music pauses while you dictate or record a call, and keeps playing with the window closed.
Settings → Appearance: describe a theme in words, preview it across the app, keep it as your own (colours and fonts), rename or delete it.
A music button at the bottom of the left bar plays calm music while you work: soft piano, lo-fi, ambient or rain, with a volume slider. On phones it's under Apps → Music.
The music pauses on its own while you take meeting notes, dictate or record a clip.
Getting started on Today asks once whether you'd like music.
New help page: Background music, with the track credits.
On a phone, choose the apps on the bottom tab bar: open Apps, tap Edit tab bar, then tap apps to add or remove them and drag to reorder. Up to five, and your choice follows you to every phone.
Hotsauce windows you leave open now switch to a new version by themselves at a quiet moment, never while you're typing or recording, and say "Hotsauce updated to" the new version.
Closing or reloading the page while dictating into a text box, using Ramble, uploading files or while a clip is still saving now asks first, so nothing is lost.
Updates itself. When a new version has downloaded, click Restart to update in the menu bar, the notification or Settings → Apps; your permissions and sign-in stay.
Sign: fix a signer's name or email after sending; their old link stops and the new address gets a fresh one, recorded in the audit trail.
Sign: copy any sent, declined or finished envelope into a new draft with the same PDF, people and fields.
Share read-only link now asks who can open it (people in your organization, or anyone with the link) and when it ends (7 days, 30 days by default, or never).
Clips can have a read-only link: people outside watch the video at any speed and read the summary and transcript, without signing in.
Files can have a link for people outside, with a preview and a download button.
The organization switch now lets members make links anyone can open, instead of opening every link at once. Links made before stay for members.
Settings → People and access lists every link, who made it and when it ends, with Turn off.
A link that has ended says so, and its Share menu offers a new one.
Dictate → Models: choose where the Mac app hears you. Online (most accurate) or On this Mac only (your voice never leaves the Mac; only the text is tidied).
Honours "On this Mac only", and its pill says "On this Mac" while it listens.
Search boxes and text fields show one orange outline when selected, not two.
The Dictate page starts with your word count, time saved, speed, top apps, this month's busy days and recent dictations. You can search them, and each one has Copy and Paste.
Dictate… in the menu bar opens that page. The separate Dictate window only appears when Hotsauce can't load, and it no longer has a Dictionary tab.
**Dropdowns look tidier.** Every dropdown now has its own arrow, set in from the edge, in both light and dark themes. Before, the browser's arrow sat right against the border.
**`/api/health` reports `features.email`.** It shows whether Sign emails signing links (both `RESEND_API_KEY` and `MAIL_FROM` set) or hands out links to copy.
Click the weather on Today to see the next 12 hours and the next 7 days, with rain or snow on the days that have more than a trace.
The meeting reminder joins the call link and starts taking notes in one click; "Just take notes" starts notes without joining.
Taking notes from the call notice starts recording right away, with no extra Start press.
When you join a call for a meeting you were reminded about, one offer replaces the other, named for the meeting.
Meeting reminders now also cover calendar events that have a call link but no other guests.
Settings: chat rooms can be switched to "Read for context", with how much is copied and when it was last read.
Search: chat messages show up in ⌘K and open in the chat.
Ask and AI tools can search and read the rooms you switched on, and the agent brief uses the last week of chat that involves you.
"Take notes on this call?" now appears even when the call app briefly lets go of the microphone as the call starts (for example when you join muted).
When an offer doesn't appear, the app records why, so it can be diagnosed.
A meeting started from the Mac app's call notice now stops on its own when the call ends, in every mode, including Mic only.
Typing in a meeting note while Enhance runs no longer jumps to New meeting when you press "c".
In the Mac app, the sound check says "The call, from apps on this Mac", keeps listening until someone speaks, and links straight to the System Audio Recording setting when the call stays silent.

**Signatures are darker and easier to read.** A typed signature is stamped on the signed PDF in blue-black ink with a slight outline, so the script reads clearly on paper. On screen it fills its field in the same ink.
**Drawn signatures** use a thicker, darker pen. The drawing is also cropped to the ink, so it fills the field instead of shrinking.

⌘, and the menu bar's Settings… open Settings → This Mac in the main window: dictation shortcut, microphone, mode, edge glow, meeting reminders, the "Take notes?" offer, open at login, menu bar icon, permissions, Run setup again, dictation history and Disconnect.
Pick which microphone dictation uses, or keep the Mac's default.
The Dictate window's Settings tab is gone; a small version opens only when Hotsauce can't load.
Settings search finds every This Mac setting inside the Mac app.
Clips: screen recordings are sharp on Retina and large screens; small text stays readable, with or without the camera bubble and after a trim.

When you connect an AI tool by signing in, you choose "Everything you can see" or "Team space only, read only". The team-only choice is for a tool many people share, like a team chat's assistant: it reads the team space only and can't change anything.
Settings → Connections marks team-only connections "Team only".
Dictate → Models shows which models hear you and tidy your words, for example "Speech: Deepgram Nova-3 · Offline: Apple, on the Mac · Cleanup: Claude Haiku 5.5".
Pick how your dictations are tidied: Fast (default), Careful (a bigger model, better with names) or Off (your exact words).
Its version now matches the Hotsauce release, and Settings only says Update available when the Mac app itself changed.
Hotsauce.work has a Download the Mac app link that always gets the newest build and shows its version.
Settings has a search box: type "dark mode", "logo" or "backup" and jump straight to that setting. Press / on any Settings page to start typing.
The command menu (⌘K) finds Settings sections too.

**Send a PDF to other people for signature.** On a draft, list who signs (inside or outside your team) and who only gets a copy. Choose whether they sign all at once or one after another, then place each person's fields and press Send.

**Signing links, no account needed.** Each signer gets their own link. It works for 30 days, and only the hash of its secret is kept. The signer opens `/signing/…`, reads the PDF, then signs or declines with a reason.
**Email through Resend** when `RESEND_API_KEY` and `MAIL_FROM` are set. Without them, Send shows each link for the sender to copy.
**Follow progress.** The envelope page shows each person's state: link sent, opened, signed, declined, or waiting for their turn. You can make a new link or email it again.
**When the last person signs,** everyone on the envelope, copies included, gets the sealed PDF and its certificate attached. Both are also saved in Files.

You can move sign-in to another Clerk application (for example from development to production) without anyone losing their clips, conversations, tokens or settings. Everyone signs in once more and carries on. See "Moving sign-in to another Clerk application" in the self-host guide.

Sign: open a PDF in Files and choose Send for signature, place signature, initials, date, text and checkbox fields, then sign by typing or drawing. A sealed signed PDF and an audit certificate are saved in Files next to the original.
Sign is in the left bar.
A task's panel, a note and a file's pop-up each keep their name at the top and × at the top right, with Delete in ⋯ More beside the ×.
A note no longer has a second "Close" button at the bottom.
A file's Rename sits in More with Delete; Download and Share stay beside the preview.
A past Briefcast episode is named in the top bar, not again in the page, and reads at a doc's width.

A clip's transcript is the page's side panel on the right, like a meeting's. It is open when you arrive on a computer, and the Transcript button at the top hides or shows it. On a phone it opens as a sheet, and choosing a line plays from there and closes it.
A saved link, a form, a check-in, a person and a company read at the same width as a doc.
A person's and a company's cards stack in one column: About, Next meeting, Open tasks, then Meetings.
Every item page names the thing once, in the top bar, with its buttons in one order: status, Share, its own buttons, then More.
One status chip: "Personal" or "Team", then "Saved". A board says "Personal" instead of "Private"; a form's Saved is no longer a red button.
Delete and downloads (CSV, Excel, clip download) live in More on every page.
A form's Questions and Answers use the list tabs; its Settings open as a pop-up from a Settings button.
A saved link's Done, Share and Delete move up into the top bar.
Tasks: switch between Inbox, Today, Upcoming, All and Done from tabs above the list, and search the list by name.
Meetings: search your meetings by name or by person from the top of the page.
Every list has the same row at the top: tabs on the left, search on the right.
Forms, Tables, Pages and Check-ins can be searched by name.
Notes, Forms, Tables and Pages have All, Personal and Team tabs.
Files can be searched on a phone.
On a phone, every page's top bar is the same: menu, title, one main button, and More for everything else
On a phone, a doc shows its name at the top instead of its file name
The Ask button no longer covers a board's undo and redo on a phone
The live demo now has Links: saved pages with reading progress, highlights and notes, an arXiv paper with its PDF, a bioRxiv paper, an added PDF and a link an AI tool saved.
Hotsauce.work has a Links card with a short video of it in action.
Sharing looks the same everywhere: a Share button with Copy link inside, in Clips, Forms, Files, Links, Notes and Boards
Boards have a Copy link of their own
Pressing Escape with a menu open closes just the menu
Pages for one thing (a form, a table, a clip, a board, a saved link, a check-in, a person) now show "‹ Forms", "‹ Tables" and so on at the top left to go back to the list.
Every pop-up has an × at its top right.
On a phone, a table's downloads and Delete are behind a "More" button so the table's name has room.
Dictation works with no connection, using speech recognition on your Mac; the pill says "Offline: on-device".
If Hotsauce can't be reached mid-dictation, what you said is written up on your Mac instead of waiting for Retry.
Every app now has its main button in the same place, at the top right: New doc, New note, New form, New table, New check-in, Save a link, Record a voice note.
New form and New table make it straight away and put the cursor in its name, so you type the name on the form or table itself.
On a phone, main buttons show their words instead of only an icon.
A doc's status now reads "Saved" instead of "Committed".

For you: one list of every comment that mentions you, with a count on the rail and a Today tile. Opening an item marks it read; Done takes it off (with Undo); Later brings it back at 9 AM tomorrow or next Monday.
For you in the Go menu.
Settings → Apps shows which Mac app version you have, and whether a newer one is out, with a Download button.
Settings → What's new lists what changed in each release, in plain words.
An "Update available" item in the menu bar menu when a newer Mac app is out.
Links keeps PDFs: save a PDF's address, press Add a PDF, or drop PDFs on Links, and you get a readable copy you can search and highlight, with the PDF itself in Files.
Papers from arXiv, bioRxiv and medRxiv show their authors, date, version, DOI and abstract, and every address of one paper is one link.
Hotsauce opens with no connection, as the last person signed in, with an Offline bar; actions that need the internet are greyed out.
Docs you type in while offline are kept on this device ("Saved on this device") and sent when you're back online, even after a reload.
Text that couldn't be sent (for example, the doc was moved meanwhile) is listed under "Kept on this device" in Docs.
Sign out works offline and takes effect when you reconnect.
On a shared computer, the next person never sees what the last one typed offline, in docs or comments.
The menu in Settings stays in place while you scroll the page.
Links: highlight passages on a saved page and add notes to them. A Highlights tab collects them, and Copy highlights to a Doc turns them into a document.
Every app shows its plain name as its title, and Whiteboard is now called Boards everywhere.
Comment on any team doc, meeting note or task. Type @ and a name to notify a teammate.
Getting started: an admin can choose which doc its last step opens.
Links uses the same screens as the other apps, and buttons use the same words everywhere (New task, New doc, Personal and Team).
A new member's Today starts with a Getting started tile: connect the calendar, get the Mac app, see the docs.
Links an AI tool saves wait for you to press Get the page.
Updates install exactly the release that was published, never a look-alike.
Clips: trim the start, the end or parts in the middle of a recording.
Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Grok by signing in, with no token to copy.
Your stars, rail pins and recent items are now part of the nightly backup.
Every app shows the same message when something couldn't load, with Try again, and the same empty screen.
Share links are made only from Share, and AI tools must read a file's latest version before changing it.
Links remembers where you stopped reading and shows how much you've read.
Settings → Usage shows admins which apps the team uses, week by week.
Settings is a few small pages (General, Connections, Apps, and Organization for admins) instead of one long scroll.
Settings is grouped by topic, and Run setup again walks through every setup step without signing you out.
One click on the Chrome extension saves the page you're on to Links.
Pin as many apps to the rail as you like.
While you dictate, a warm glow hugs the edges of the window you're typing into.
Links keeps a copy of the page as you saw it when you save it from Chrome.
